title: How Sounds Are Made
seo_title: Year 4 Science: How Sounds Are Made Worksheets (Vibrations and Hearing)
standard_text: Identify how sounds are made, associating some of them with something vibrating. Recognise that vibrations from sounds travel through a medium to the ear.
meta_desc: Free Year 4 science worksheets on how sounds are made: vibrations, how sound travels through solids, liquids and gases, the ear, the speed of sound, echoes and string telephones. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Every sound starts with a vibration.
key_sub: Vibrations travel through solids, liquids and gases to our ears.
body_html:
How to think about it

Sounds are made when something vibrates.

  • The vibrations travel through a solid, liquid or gas to our ears. Sound cannot travel through empty space.
  • In the ear, the eardrum vibrates, tiny bones pass the vibrations on, and nerves send messages to the brain.
  • Sound travels about 340 m per second in air: much slower than light. An echo is sound reflected back.
Example

What vibrates in a recorder?

The player blows air into the tube

Answer: the air inside

Example

Echo after 2 seconds. Cliff distance?

340 × 2 = 680 m there and back

680 ÷ 2

Answer: 340 m

Common mistakes

  • Thinking sound can travel through empty space.
  • Thinking sound is faster than light.
  • Thinking a slack string telephone works best.

faq.a: Every sound is made by something vibrating, such as a guitar string, a drum skin, the air in a recorder or your vocal cords.

faq.q: How does sound reach our ears?
faq.a: The vibrations pass through a medium, such as air, water or a solid, into the ear, where the eardrum vibrates and the brain hears the sound.
No. Space is almost empty, so there are no particles to carry the vibrations.
